newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India rallies on Bajaj earnings.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India rallies on Bajaj earnings.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) rallied on Thursday on the back of positive earnings from scooter-maker Bajaj Auto.
"The results from Bajaj gave the market a filip, people have been expecting a slowdown and these were well ahead of expectations," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI rose 1.17 points, 1.94 percent, to 61.35 points, with the premium over the local market at 10.57 percent compared with yesterday's 8.41 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 9.20 points, or 0.29 percent, to 3,163.78, but bounced off an earlier low of 3,122.76.
Bajaj reported a 27 percent rise in first half net profit to 2.26 billion rupees, ahead of expectations, and its shares rose 14.75 rupees, or 1.56 percent, to 956.25 on the BSE.
Its GDR followed suit, adding $1.83 to $31.50/$32.50.
Vehicle maker Mahindra & Mahindra first half net profit rose to 924.30 million rupees from 738.10 million a year ago, its GDRs fell 37 cents to $9.50/$10.50.

ITC GDRs continued under pressure after chairman Yogesh Deveshwar was called in to the office of the Enforcement Directorate a day after the government announced an investigation into alleged foreign exchange rule violations by the cigarette maker.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.14 points at 64.45, a premium of 27 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index closed half a poiny up at a provisional 757.59.
A holiday in Taiwan saw the Capel Taiwan GDR Index end just 0.23 points higher at 87.17, a premium of 1.91 percent.
